items.title: GW250114 reveals signatures of post-merger black-hole horizon
items.summary: The observation of a direct wave after the merger of two black holes reveals signatures associated with the remnant black-hole horizon, establishing an observational channel to directly measure frame-dragging effects in black-hole ergospheres and probe the horizon surface gravity.

items.title: Detection of anisotropic cosmic structures on a gigaparsec scale
items.summary: Using the parameter-free Angular Distribution of Pairwise Distances for measuring directional correlations, evidence is found for coherent anisotropic structures extending over gigaparsec scales, challenging the assumption that the Universe becomes statistically isotropic on sufficiently large scales.

items.title: Zero-shot design of drug-binding proteins via neural iterative selection−expansion
items.summary: By pairing two neural networks in an iterative optimization algorithm, small-molecule binding proteins can be designed from scratch with high accuracy, affinity and success rates, showing promise for applications in drug delivery and sequestration.

items.title: Global high-resolution mapping of seagrass to support conservation
items.summary: Global high-resolution mapping shows widespread seagrass loss and degradation since 2019, with most meadows outside protected areas, highlighting urgent conservation and climate-policy needs.

items.title: An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning
items.summary: A deep-learning model trained on electrocardiogram (ECG) waveforms identifies an easily visible biomarker that predicts sudden cardiac death more accurately than the current clinical state of the art.

items.title: A Streptomyces megacluster encodes synergistic biotin-targeting antibiotics
items.summary: In Streptomyces spp., a conserved biosynthetic gene megacluster produces an arsenal of distinct antimicrobials that converge on bacterial biotin biosynthesis as a naturally evolved combination therapy.

items.title: Genomic insights into the population dynamics and demise of Neanderthals
items.summary: A surge of genetic data from the skeletal remains of Neanderthals disproves some assumptions and generates fresh questions about these ancient hominins.

items.title: A hidden predictor of sudden cardiac death uncovered by deep learning
items.summary: A machine-learning model trained on thousands of electrocardiogram recordings identifies a previously unrecognized group of at-risk people.

items.title: A global map of seagrass ecosystems
items.summary: Combining satellite imagery and machine learning has created the first comprehensive map of seagrass meadows, in a boost for the conservation of these crucial ecosystems.

items.title: Medical records could be revealed by AI training-data vulnerability
items.summary: Identification risks are more severe for underrepresented groups in the training data — plus, evidence that the Universe is more uneven than assumed.

items.title: AI tool spots antibiotics that fight drug-resistant gonorrhoea
items.summary: The bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae has evolved resistance to most antibiotics used to treat it, but a machine-learning screen reveals potential therapies.

items.title: Genetic technologies to enhance crop nutritional value under climate change
items.summary: This Review reflects on the joint power of genetic technologies, including untapped CRISPR–Cas techniques to combat hidden hunger and improve crop resilience, and argues in favour of their combined use to overcome these societal challenges.

items.title: Immunological mechanisms of mRNA vaccines for infectious diseases
items.summary: A Review of the immunological mechanisms of mRNA–lipid-nanoparticle vaccines for infectious diseases discusses how the components of this vaccine platform can be modified to fine-tune immune responses against challenging pathogens.

items.title: Alternate RNA decoding results in stable and abundant proteins in mammals
items.summary: Alternate RNA decoding, an understudied process, leads to peptide sequence modifications that can have substantial functional effects on protein stability, tissue-specific proteomes and disease.

items.title: Antibiotic cocktail made by soil bacteria can kill superbugs
items.summary: Four antibiotic compounds produced in Streptomyces bacteria attack multiple parts of an essential metabolic pathway.

items.title: Epiblast diversification and blood formation in a human pregastrula
items.summary: High-resolution spatial transcriptome analysis of a human embryo at Carnegie stage 6 reveals three distinct developmental trajectories from the epiblast towards amnion, primitive streak and axial mesoderm, and detects the initiation of haematopoiesis before gastrulation, originating from hypoblast rather than epiblast.

items.title: Chiral laser gyroscopes breaking the lock-in limit
items.summary: Ring laser gyroscope lock-in has been eliminated using spontaneous symmetry breaking in a He–Ne laser, enabling accurate near-zero rotation sensing without external components, improving miniaturization and precision.

items.title: ‘Megacluster’ of genes enables bacteria to make potent antibiotic mixture
items.summary: Soil bacteria make cocktails of molecules that synergistically inhibit the growth of microbial pathogens — suggesting a strategy for tackling antibiotic-resistant infections.

items.title: The mutational landscape of STING-induced immunity
items.summary: A massively parallel assay systematically charts the sequence-function landscape of the STING signalling protein, and the findings define molecular principles that tune STING activity and show its functional potential across immune contexts.

items.title: Dietary cholesterol activates a Ral-dependent pathway driving LDLR turnover
items.summary: Chronic dietary cholesterol activates Ral GTPases, which promote LDLR internalization and lysosomal degradation through RalBP1–REPS1 and CTSA, thereby reducing cholesterol clearance, whereas CTSA inhibition restores LDLR function and may offer a therapeutic strategy for cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Ductile alloys offering 100 MPa tensile strength at 2,400 °C
items.summary: A boron-stabilized oxide-strengthened tantalum alloy combines exceptional room-temperature ductility with record ultrahigh-temperature strength, enabling load-bearing applications above 2,000 °C.

items.title: Long-sought chemical inhibitors of β-arrestin proteins
items.summary: Proteins called β-arrestins regulate signalling through members of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) superfamily. Small molecules that bind directly to the β-arrestins and inhibit their activities are the first chemical tools to probe their biology, opening avenues for transducer-targeted, pathway-specific GPCR therapeutics.

items.title: Small-molecule modulation of β-arrestins
items.summary: Integrated pharmacological, biochemical, biophysical and structural analyses of small-molecule β-arrestin inhibitors show how they block β-arrestin engagement with activated GPCRs, revealing their mechanism of action and uncovering a previously unrecognized allosteric regulatory site.

items.title: Genetic diversity of late Neanderthals in northwestern Europe
items.summary: Genetic sequencing of multiple late Neanderthals living less than 52,500 years ago provides an overview of genetic diversity and demonstrates that even low-coverage nuclear genome data can increase resolution of within-Neanderthal diversity.

items.title: Crude oil turns cheap porous membrane into a sieve to refine itself without heat
items.summary: An inexpensive, porous polymer membrane helps to separate raw crude oil, without heat or selective coating. Heavy hydrocarbons self-assemble inside the pores to create channels that are likely to be less than 2 nanometres wide, enriching the resulting permeate mix into light, ‘naphtha range’ hydrocarbons with 30% less energy cost and carbon dioxide emissions than conventional distillation.

items.title: How long-term dietary cholesterol can slow down its own clearance by liver cells
items.summary: Cholesterol carried by low-density lipoprotein (LDL) drives heart disease and is cleared by liver cells expressing the receptor LDLR. A cell-signalling mechanism has been discovered through which high cholesterol promotes the enzyme-mediated degradation of LDLR. Blocking this enzyme restores LDLR levels in liver cells, suggesting a new strategy for treating high cholesterol.

items.title: Disparate privacy risks from medical AI
items.summary: AI models for medical diagnostics are vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

items.title: Crude oil fractionation by means of mesoporous polyacrylonitrile membranes
items.summary: Porous polyacrylonitrile membranes—typically used as non-selective support layers—can be used to achieve effective molecular refining of crude oil at steady state, enabling substantial reductions in energy consumption, cooling water, and CO2 emissions compared with distillation processes.

items.title: Laser light switches on heat flow in ultra-thin structures
items.summary: A temperature difference of more than 100 kelvin can be created between stacked layers of 2D material by irradiating them with laser light.

items.title: Silicon Valley’s vision for global AI is flawed: each country needs its own blueprint
items.summary: From energy grids to language performance, emerging economies are exposing the limits of today’s artificial-intelligence strategy as it expands globally.

items.title: Optical cooling by interfacial charge transfer in 2D heterostructures
items.summary: Optical cooling in two-dimensional semiconductor heterostructures is demonstrated through phonon-assisted interfacial charge transfer, enabling cryogen-free thermal management without stringent quantum-efficiency requirements.

items.title: Fourier pixels for bidirectional light control
items.summary: A versatile platform of miniaturized Fourier-optics-based diffractive elements enables multifunctional pixels that fully control and sense the amplitude, phase and polarization of optical wavefronts for advanced photonic applications.

items.title: Daily briefing: Sperm whales have different dialects
items.summary: Whales in different areas of the Mediterranean use varying patterns of clicks and pauses. Plus, a technique to make protein samples one billion times bigger and the science of grief.

items.summary: Carbon dioxide bubbling up from underground material can solidify into formations of up to five metres tall.

items.summary: From AI to biotechnology, today’s scientific breakthroughs raise ethical and social challenges that technical expertise alone cannot solve.

items.title: ‘Us’ not ‘them’: scientists must use their skills to help stop polarization and division

items.summary: The scientific community awaits a patent for recombinant DNA technology, and experimentation with an anaesthetic from puffballs, in our weekly dip into Nature’s archive.
